<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/embedder-openai`, `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **133** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/LICENSE`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/LICENSE`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **42** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa9fb984ef7431186b9c71300a607182c6d3f238` — the merge of head `4ab06c2f0ab82479938696301e70d1ad0ef44435` into base `c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa9fb984ef7431186b9c71300a607182c6d3f238 && git checkout fa9fb984ef7431186b9c71300a607182c6d3f238
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440 4ab06c2f0ab82479938696301e70d1ad0ef44435 && git checkout -B drift-repro c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440 && git merge --no-ff 4ab06c2f0ab82479938696301e70d1ad0ef44435

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c2f8bff93f6484c43b7667955a0a3541c1454440` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 结论:这单先不合,退回补一轮。功能方向和接口都对(自建部署用自己的 PostgreSQL 做向量检索;换了嵌入模型或切分方式后旧索引被明确拒绝),对已有适配器(含 cloud 的 turso)没有破坏。
- 要改的:两处会误导运维——嵌入服务没配好时,系统会把一个健康的索引报成「需要重建并删除」;提示的清理 SQL 不完整,照着只跑一半会让旧向量混进新索引。另外 #37335 已先落地,本单要合并主干并补两项返回字段,否则真数据库上的用例会红。
- 证据缺口:真数据库上的 41 个用例在 PR 上不跑,只在合并队列里跑,且红了也不拦;目前只有开发者本机一份结果,需要在分支上补一次完整 CI。
- 需要你做的:现在不用。修完后再审一轮;届时因改了 CI 文件且超过 3000 行,仍需你批准。接口放置问题(searchWithRefusals)建议本单维持现状,是否进正式接口留给你定。

## 席位核对

REWORK — the contract members are the ones ADR-0161 K8 accepted and are additive-safe, but five items are open at this head: two defects in the store's refusal path, a merge of `main` that the store owes two hit keys to, one false changeset sentence, and no CI reading of the live suites. Nothing is armed; the PR stays draft.

Head-sha: `4ab06c2f0ab82479938696301e70d1ad0ef44435`

Read whole: 45 files, +3495 / -94, nine commits on `dbc1765a`. Head re-read at the end of the review: unchanged.

**形态**
- Open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #37100`, the only closing keyword in the body. Body and changeset read `Clause-②: yes` · `Metadata-protocol: none`; all five packages `patch`, which is the level `none` takes. `Skills-docs:` not owed. `l1-face.mjs --pr 37337`: every mechanical item ok.
- Governed, Tier H: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 37337` reads 1 of 45 paths on the register (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, Tier H by content: the new build step copies the job's four `TURBO_*` lines), and 3589 changed lines, over the 3000 line. Either alone makes it a human merge.
- `mergeable_state: dirty` since #37335 merged as `38017753`. A test merge with `origin/main` at `a182fbe3` conflicts in `knowledge-service.ts`, `testing.ts` and `knowledge-memory/src/index.ts`.
- File surface against the claim: inside it, with three additions that a gate or the ledger forces and that are accepted below (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 46, the generated reference pages and spec baselines).

**门禁 check-runs** (at `4ab06c2f`, read twice, last after the review)
- 64 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates: success. TypeScript Type Check: success. The 11 skips are the expected names.
- `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is one of the skips: the job never runs on `pull_request`. The two steps this PR adds have not run in CI at any head.
- Local at `4ab06c2f`, scratch worktree, removed: `service-knowledge` 291/291 (12 files), `knowledge-memory` 43/43, `embedder-openai` 31/31, `knowledge-pgvector` 7 passed and 41 skipped without a URL; `vitest run live-postgres` selects the three live files (41 cases); with `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1` and no URL, 3 named failures. The 41 live cases: NOT MEASURED here (this container has PostgreSQL 16 without the `vector` extension).

**逐项核对与消融** (12 single-change ablations, tree restored each time)
1. Coded refusal collected in `searchRound` — off: 2 red in `service-knowledge`, 2 red in the memory contract run.
2. `beginBuild` before a complete walk — off: 2 red (memory contract run). `completeBuild` after it — off: 3 red.
3. The search carries `index` — off: 2 + 3 red. The whole refusal is thrown — off: 1 + 2 red.
4. `knowledge-memory` refuses a search under another fingerprint — off: 4 red; a write — off: 1 red.
5. `search_knowledge` adds `refused` — off: 1 red. The fingerprint covers `variant` — off: 2 red (the pinned digest and the five-component case).
6. The not-ready refusal carries the SQL — off: 1 red (`not-ready.test.ts`).
7. Two paths are not pinned by any suite that runs on a PR: a refused `beginBuild` answering `ok: false` (swallowed: all green; its one pin is a live case), and a `completeBuild` that throws (swallowed: all green; no pin at all).
- Refusal cases assert `code` and `status` (the suite's `expectRebuildRefusal`, the tool cases, the not-ready cases).
- The `embedder-openai` case cannot fail at run time without the change (the property existed, private); its pin is the type check.

**完成标准对卡** (#37100, ten items, six acceptance lines)
- Delivered as written: 1, 2 (with `title`, `heading_path`, `recipe_hash` beyond the list, stated), 3, 5, 7, 8, 10; K8 item 8 whole, as scope note 7145595033 asks; the reindex case over a real driver from 7145881825.
- Item 4 and item 6 are delivered with the two defects in the fix list (items 1 and 2).
- Item 9 and acceptance line 6 ("passes in CI on real PostgreSQL"): wired, not yet observed (item 5).

**CI 改动** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, +32 / -2)
- The claim's condition holds: on the base, the job's steps name `driver-sql`, the non-SQL backends, `metadata-protocol` and `runtime`; none runs this package, and Test Core runs it without a URL (a named skip).
- Size: a build step and a run step shaped as the runtime leg above them, the step-count comment, and one `temporal_live` path. The secret references are the job's own four lines, copied. No smaller edit runs the suite; dropping the `TURBO_*` lines would not lower the tier, because the size line holds it at a human merge.
- The one discretionary line is `service-knowledge/src/testing.ts` in `temporal_live`: every queue entry that touches the contract suite now starts the job (#37342 does). Accepted: a change to the suite is a change to that step's verdict.
- What the edit does not give: a required check. The job is advisory in the queue, so a red there lands and shows on `main`.

**逐句核的散文面**
- Changeset: false — `indexExpectation` is listed among the new exports of `@objectstack/service-knowledge` and `src/index.ts` does not export it. Imprecise — "the platform's when `OS_DATABASE_URL` is PostgreSQL, else the `url` option": the code takes `url` first. The other sentences are true of the code.
- `README.md`, `protocol/knowledge.mdx` 4.1, `ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`, the plugin's TSDoc: the same inverted precedence. `knowledge-rag.mdx` says the service "computes and checks" the fingerprint (the adapter checks). 4.1 says one generation row "per source and fingerprint" (the key is source and generation). The plugin option's TSDoc says the kernel embedder is "read at each call"; it is cached after the first read.
- `system-context.mdx` row 46 and its census line: true. Generated reference pages and spec baselines: regenerated, gates green.

**接受的偏差**
- `beginBuild` under another fingerprint is refused, not built beside the first: the card puts the second generation out of scope (#37101).
- The store reads `OS_DATABASE_URL` / `DATABASE_URL`, not a datasource declared in code; such a stack passes `url`. Stated.
- The store takes no builder lock; a rebuild is in place. #37101 owns the lock with the second generation.
- `Clause-②: yes` carries no arm; `(widening)` would also be valid.
- Between this PR and #37099, a changed fingerprint (a source's content list, `split`, the `chunk_target` setting, the embedder) takes a source's search down until someone runs a complete reindex; on this store, hand SQL first. K7 rules 4 and 5 as written.

**范围外去向**
- #37342 (#37308) edits the same `search()`, `testing.ts` and `knowledge-memory`; the third to land merges `main` again and owes `scope` on this store.
- #37304 changes the store's keying (ruling 7168239918); nothing built for it here.
- Open question (4): see ③. The interface member is the maintainer's to decide; if it is taken up, it is a dated note on ADR-0161 and its own card.

**落地条款**
- Clause-② declared and the path limb hit: the contract record below is FAIL at this head. No auto-merge is armed and no label is hung by this record.
- After the fix list: a fresh record on the new head (the merge of `main` moves more than prose), every check green or an expected skip, a CI reading of the two new steps at that head, then `pm:awaiting-merge` and the maintainer's approval (Tier H).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4ab06c2f0ab82479938696301e70d1ad0ef44435`
Local-runs: probe — four package suites, 12 ablations and two database-double probes in a scratch worktree, to learn which changes a test pins and to confirm two refusal paths; nothing was pushed, and the live PostgreSQL files could not be run here.
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-index-fingerprint.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-tools.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/testing.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/split/splitter.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/pgvector-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/sql.ts, packages/plugins/embedder-openai/src/index.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Every new member is in the K8 table in its decided shape. Item 8 a: `AdapterContext.index?` with `fingerprint` and `recipeHash`; `AdapterSearchOptions.index?` with `fingerprint`. Item 8 b: `indexStatus?(ctx)` answering `fingerprint?`, `recipeHash?`, `building?`. Item 8 c: `beginBuild?(ctx)` and `completeBuild?(ctx)`. Item 7: `IEmbedder.model?`. Item 6: the descriptor's `model?`, `dimensions?`, `variant?`, which item 6 assigns to the PR that lands item 8. No member outside the table; item 13 and item 17 untouched.
- `AdapterIndexExpectation` and `AdapterIndexStatus` are type names for those shapes, not members in K8's sense. `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` is a ledger code for the refusal K7 rules 4 and 5 call for; the ADR fixes no name.
- Rule 1 holds: each member lands with its reader (the service, `knowledge-memory` as reference, the store) and with suite cases; the Execution note ("item 8 lands whole, once") is met, including the pair case.
- Rule 2 holds: every member is optional. An adapter without them is called as before, is handed `index` and may ignore it. Read in the tree and in `objectstack-ai/cloud` (code search plus the local checkout at `d2c4981`): `KnowledgeRagflowAdapter`, cloud's `TursoKnowledgeAdapter` and `HashEmbedder` implement none of the new members and compile unchanged; no cloud class holds a private `model` beside `implements IEmbedder`; nothing in cloud names `searchWithRefusals`, `indexStatus` or `beginBuild`.
- One behaviour moves for every caller of `KnowledgeService.search`: a source whose adapter throws an error with a SCREAMING `code` and a 4xx/5xx `status` is no longer logged and read as empty; when no source answers, the call throws. K7 rule 5 asks for it and the changeset says it. `knowledge-ragflow` and the libSQL client throw no such shape; cloud's own `search_knowledge` handler catches and reports the message.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on all five packages: the level the kind takes (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). No metadata key, accepted value or metadata type is added; the members are adapter-contract members, not authorable keys.
- No narrowing: nothing published is removed or refused that was accepted. `OpenAIEmbedder.model` goes from private to public.
- The changeset names an export that does not exist (`indexExpectation`): must-fix, below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (4), `searchWithRefusals` on the class: K9 rule 3 is kept (`search` unchanged), and K7 rule 5 makes #37100 the proposer. Recommendation: keep A in this PR. It adds nothing to `IKnowledgeService`, so no dated note is owed, and the one tool definition reads it. Its cost is a silent seam: a service that wraps or proxies `IKnowledgeService` loses the named refusals and falls back to hits alone (the whole refusal still throws, the partial one is only logged). B is the durable shape before cloud's in-app agent (row 13) or the first wrapper reads refusals; it is a member on a published contract and so the maintainer's decision, by a dated note. Escalated as a decision, not answered here.
- Dev flag, the CI edit: answered in the seat section. Justified by the claim's condition; kept in this PR.
- Dev flag, the overlap with #37335: it merged first. See ④, must-fix 3.
- SQL push-down: the organization filter, the metadata filter and the ranking are one statement; listing pages in SQL; the unchanged-passage read is one statement per batch. No id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could do it. Writes are one statement per passage inside one transaction: a cost, not a finding.
- Security read: SQL construction (identifiers, values, the width-derived table name, filter keys), tenant isolation on every read path, the not-ready text and logs. No finding on injection or on the organization wall. Three findings on what refusal text carries and to whom, graded below without mechanism; specifics are in the seat reply.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts`
- Holds against K7 and K8 item 8, and against its first consumers. The `beginBuild` text adds "or, when it cannot, refuses with a coded refusal": within K7 rule 3, which already has the adapter refuse a second builder.
- nit — "The adapter keeps one builder per source" is not yet true of the store; #37101.
- Design gap the first persisting consumer shows: the descriptor is read at each call, and a store whose embedder is not registered at that moment reports none, so the service hands it a fingerprint that differs from the stored one. The text treats an absent descriptor as a property of the adapter (K7 rule 8), not of the moment. The repair is in the store (must-fix 1); one sentence here would help the next store (#37107).

`packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts`
- Holds: item 7 as decided, `id` stays a log label.

`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`
- Holds: one code under the three packages that stamp or assert it; gates green.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Holds as wiring (seat section). It gives an advisory reading, not a gate.

`packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/pgvector-adapter.ts`
- must-fix 1 — `search` compares the fingerprint before it resolves the embedder. With no embedder registered (the boot window, or the embedder unset in settings) a healthy index is refused `409 KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` with the instruction to drop it, where `upsert` and `beginBuild` answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, no embedder. Confirmed with a database double. The wrong code, and a remedy that deletes a good index.
- must-fix 2 — the clear-the-source remedy. The text is one runnable statement (the generation row) and a prose description of the second with a placeholder table name. A source whose generation row is gone while its passage rows remain is taken up by the next first generation under the same number; the complete reindex then lists those rows and skips every document whose hash is unchanged, so vectors of the old fingerprint are served under the new one (K7 rule 1, and the card's "old rows not served"). Owed: exact statements (the width is known), passages before the generation row, and a first generation that never adopts rows left under its number; a live case for it.
- should-fix — an unreachable database is reported as "extension not installed" with the DDL, and the driver's own error text rides in the coded refusal to the caller.
- should-fix — the search-path refusal hands operator text to the tool's caller; a caller needs the code and a sentence, the operator text belongs to the reindex result, the log and `healthCheck`.
- should-fix — the unchanged-passage `UPDATE` is not checked for a row; under a concurrent rewrite of the same document a passage can go missing, and the document-hash skip then hides it.
- nit — one identifier is quoted without doubling an embedded quote (a value a database owner sets).

`packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/plugin.ts`
- should-fix — the kernel embedder is cached after the first read; a re-registered embedder (a settings change) is not seen until restart, against the option's own text and K8 item 6.
- should-fix — the pool has no connection timeout; boot awaits `healthCheck`, so an unreachable host stalls boot and every call for the system's TCP timeout.
- should-fix — two deployments on one database share the default schema, keyed by source id alone; one sentence in the README (set `schema`), until #37304 changes the key.

`packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/sql.ts`
- Holds: the schema is held to a lower-case identifier at construction, the width to a positive integer, every value is bound.

`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts`
- Holds against K7 rules 3 and 5: one plan per walk, the pair around a complete walk only, neither call under `limit` or `dryRun`, the refused sources named, the whole refusal only when none answers.
- must-fix 3 — merge `main` (#37335 is in). Both intents on `search`: the record-level answer and its freshness repair from `main`, the refusal report from this PR; every adapter call `main` added (the repair's `upsert` and `delete`) carries `index`. On `main` the suite asserts `docHash` on a hit under `listDocuments` and `headingPath` under `chunks`; the store declares both, so its hits must carry both (it already stores them), or the live contract run is red in a job that does not eject.
- should-fix — two stub cases here: a refused `beginBuild` (`ok: false`, no listing, no write) and a `completeBuild` that throws (`ok: false`). Today neither is pinned on a PR.
- nit — a source refused in the refill round is named in `refused` while its first-round hits stay in the answer.
- nit — `planIndex` reads the chunk-target setting once per source per search.

`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-index-fingerprint.ts`
- Holds against K7: five components, values in sorted-key JSON, pinned digests, `where` and `metadataFields` left to the recipe hash (point 2). `maxTokens` rides in the resolved split: it is a value that cuts the text.

`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-tools.ts`
- Holds against K9 rules 1 to 3: one definition, `refused` limited to the sources the caller may see, `search` unchanged.

`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/testing.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/split/splitter.ts`, `packages/plugins/embedder-openai/src/index.ts`
- Hold. Nine new cases, each red under its ablation; the reference keeps an active generation and one under construction and switches at `completeBuild`.

Findings open at this head: five must-fix (three above; the false changeset export; the CI reading of the live suites at the landing head), eight should-fix (seven above; the inverted database precedence in the prose faces), six nits (four above; two prose sentences in the seat section).

Implemented-by: `session_01JQwxbX5BF433x8ooJNQVRp`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbW5anP6GDaVi5LKi2U`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
